causalAutopsy.notes: The test-runner floor (ACT-069) was built to stop a busy suite being judged at ~190s, and it fixed that. Its expiry was never designed: one hour of wall clock, chosen as 'generous', with nothing checking health at the boundary. Because the hard ceiling is 30 minutes, the moment the floor lapses every fail-closed path already votes to interrupt, so the hour mark is not a handover to judgement but a scheduled kill for any run that long. Latent from the floor's introduction until a full suite genuinely needed more than an hour on a saturated machine (2026-10-20, 3610s), with a second instance the same night on a git push running a pre-push tier (3615s).
